Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won. Two information roles decided the game. Carol (Chronicler) marked Erin on Night 1, so Erin was revealed as a Scout, a true anchor result. Carol then marked Bob on Night 2, which made hanging him safe: he was revealed as Talent Agent, a Yakuza role. Olivia's Night 2 census of Bob, Ivan and Judy found 1 Evil. Together with Ivan's will, which named his chosen pair of Bob and Carol, that left the Village sure about Bob even though Ivan was killed before he could post the result. On Day 2, Heidi's archive named Census Taker, Fortune Teller and Scout before anyone had claimed them. That made her credible, so Ivan's random Seer pair (Mallory and Heidi have different alignments) got Mallory hanged at 12–0. Mallory's late Zealot reveal and her "Heidi could be Neutral" argument changed no votes. The Yakuza hurt themselves early. Bob held his claim back all day, then claimed Enforcer, a role from Heidi's list, with a "visit" to the one player whose visit data was already public. Nearly everyone named that as the weakest fit. Judy (Executioner, target Bob) pushed Bob from Day 2 with no data, claimed Juror (Astral, so it can't be checked) only once Bob was on trial, and won when he was hanged. Her revenge killed Olivia, and Olivia's Bonded partner Carol died of heartbreak. On Night 3, Grace used her Diviner action on herself for Strong Defense, which was clever. She survived the hitback from Dave's trap, and the same trap stopped her Katana attack on Olivia. Niaj then wasted his Armed shot on Heidi, a Good Archivist. He acted on Ivan's pair even though hanging Mallory had already explained it. On Day 4, Alice used her Sniper shot well. Grace had publicly said Guilty on Frank and the total was exactly 3, so Grace was the only Guilty vote not explained by Bob and Mallory. Grace had also left a "held my track" gap on Night 2. Alice killed her with a Strong shot. Frank, the Arsonist, doused three players but never ignited. All his Tracker results were "visited nobody" on players who never visit, and a nomination by Niaj got him hanged as the last bad player.
Moderator (claude-opus-5.5) lessons · $0.0000
Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: high, harness bugBob was a Talent Agent with the Disguised trait (shown as Enforcer). Carol marked him on Night 2, and when he was hanged on Day 3 the reveal said 'Talent Agent'. The Chronicler's reveal is an exact-role check, and R19 says exact-role checks see a Disguised player's disguise, so it should have shown Enforcer. The game also handled the disguise inconsistently: Heidi's Night 1 Archivist result correctly showed Enforcer for Bob. The wrong reveal settled the game's central question and broke a plan the Yakuza had built on their reading of the rules.
Review: medium, rules ambiguityThe Chronicler text says a marked player's death 'reveals their true role to everyone (an exact-role check, R19)'. 'True role' conflicts with R19, which says exact-role checks see a disguise. This probably caused the wrong reveal of Bob. The text should say outright that a Disguised player's disguise is shown.
Review: medium, player confusionBecause of the wrong reveal, players drew false conclusions. Heidi's and Carol's wills said the Enforcer on Heidi's list was a fake that Bob had borrowed, when it was really his disguise showing up in an exact-role check. Heidi went on to say that at least 3 claimants were lying.
Review: low, moderator errorCarol was told 'You were attacked tonight (heartbreak) and died.' Under the Bonded trait, heartbreak isn't an attack, so the message should not call it one.
Review: low, prompt problemAt setup the program logged a tips_stale error: the tips file had been checked against an older version of the rules. All 13 players were still given it, so they may have read tips that no longer hold.
Review: low, harness bugThe moderator summaries contain internal notes (the Night 2 summary says 'The held tell() to Dave only described his own trap placement, so nothing needed resending'), and the Night 1 summary was printed twice. No player saw these, but they make the log harder to read.
Review: low, player confusionFrank's Day 4 claim reads 'D2: Innocent on Mallory? no: Guilty on Mallory'. He corrected himself inside the claim text, which suggests the claim tool gives no clean way to fix a mistake.
Game over
WinnersAlice, Carol, Dave, Erin, Heidi, Ivan, Niaj, Olivia, Judy
